subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron jobs get a dedicated `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or wait for the broader per-session tool-policy design?
rationale: The source-backed gap is real, but adding or inheriting a public config/security surface changes operator semantics and tool-policy precedence, which repository policy treats as maintainer-owned product/security direction.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence and docs/tests for cron isolated sessions and delivery modes.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat cron isolated sessions as covered by `tools.subagents.tools`, reducing new config surface but coupling two different runtime concepts.

options.title: Wait for per-session policy
options.body: Fold this into the broader per-session tool-policy RFC and keep cron-specific mitigations limited to delivery behavior until that design lands.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence and docs/tests for cron isolated sessions and delivery modes.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior issue review by steipete is the clearest available routing signal for the cron/config/tool-policy decision surface.
